messages.author: 2965834ac131c001
messages.subject: installation trouble
parts:
Hi all,

I attempted to install ggplot2, as recommended, using install.packages
("ggplot2"). However, I received the warning message 'In
install.packages("ggplot2") : package 'ggplot2' is not available.'

I read a couple discussions here, where users had had similar
problems. One suggestion was to update the installation of R, which I
did. To no avail.

Using the command install.packages(), I was presented with a list of
available packages at the mirror I had selected. ggplot2 was not on
the list. It went ... ggm, GGMselect, gibbs.met ...

BTW, my OS is Ubuntu 8.04. As a test, I tried installing another
package from the list. It installed with no errors.

Any suggestions?

Thanks,
Ryan

messages.author: 2965834ac131c001
messages.subject: Re: installation trouble
parts:
Hadley et al.,

I believe the problem may be my installation of Ubuntu, which is
relatively old. Although I updated R using apt-get, thinking I would
receive the latest version of R, I still only have R version 2.6.2 ...
as seen in the following text dump from sessionInfo(). Apparently, I
cannot get a newer version of R with the older version of ubuntu.

-----------------------------------------
R version 2.6.2 (2008-02-08)
i486-pc-linux-gnu

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] rcompgen_0.1-17
------------------------------------------

So, I am currently updating to ubuntu 10.04 (Lucid Lynx), which
supposedly includes R 2.9.2. I'm guessing this will solve the problem,
but it takes about an hour to update. I will report back with the
results.

Sorry I didn't realize this earlier and hope I didn't waste anyone's
time. As a data graphics enthusiast, I'm really looking forward to
using ggplot2.

Ryan
